analyst_view.overall: Early view: Bournemouth are flying with eight straight wins in all competitions but play Brighton three days before and have a Europa League schedule, having played nine games in a month. Hull have drawn three of their last five and defended compactly for over an hour at Arsenal before losing 1-0. Bournemouth should dominate, but Hull will make it awkward.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. I lean slightly lower: Hull kept Arsenal to one goal and their games rarely open up, and their main creator Mohamed Belloumi is injured. Bournemouth may also rotate after the Brighton game, which tends to slow down their attack.

corners.text: The site has 10.1 corners, 6.5 for Bournemouth. I lean higher: Hull sit in a deep back five and Bournemouth attack down the wings, so blocked crosses and shots should bring many corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. I agree: Hull will foul to slow Bournemouth's quick attacks, and they had a player suspended for the Arsenal game. Nothing points clearly higher or lower.

shots.text: The site has 27.5 shots. I agree: Bournemouth will take a lot of shots against a deep side, and Hull will offer little in return, as their 8.3 away shots suggest. Rotation is the only reason it could drop.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. I lean lower: Hull block a lot and keep the shots from distance, and Arsenal needed a rebound to beat them. Fewer on target than the figure.
